evidence: Judged against the shipped format per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 (the internal 'Likert we dont use' note is the documented false positive). Type census of the frozen task: (1) Gates: render/judge.toml:20 hro_gate_render and constraints/judge.toml:20 hro_gate_shared are type="binary" with aggregation all_pass, matching Deterministic C33's binary-only gate rule. (2) Functional: all 44 criteria (hro_job_open ... hro_restart, functional/judge.toml:23-408) are type="binary"; each describes a discrete observable pass/fail outcome with an explicit 'Fails if ...' clause (e.g. :110 'Fails if Interview can hold more cards than places', :200 stale-move refusal naming the person). None grades degree of quality, so binary fits. (3) Polish: 5 criteria (polish/judge.toml:17-60) are type="binary": live-board edit preservation, live-thread draft/focus, earlier-messages anchor position, failed-send retention/no duplicate, ended-session prompt. These are state-preservation behaviours that either hold or not (draft text equal, document.activeElement unchanged, nothing sent twice); the template's polish dimension is likewise binary (template polish/judge.toml:20,31,42,52). Not craft criteria, so binary does not lose gradation. (4) Visual: 5 criteria hro_vis_type/color/layout/hierarchy/consistency (visual/judge.toml:18-90) are type="likert", points=5, each with a described anchor on every level 5,4,3,2,1 (e.g. :25-29). These are craft/degree-of-quality judgements and are correctly likert. The task drops the template's extra '0' anchor (template visual/judge.toml:33 etc.) and instead uses 1..5, which matches points=5 and the RewardKit 'integer from 1 to 5' hint the template prompt mentions (template visual/prompt.md:39-41); the task visual prompt is internally consistent with that scale: ':7 lowest score (binary 0; Likert 1)', ':12 minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero ... grade every criterion independently with its five anchors', ':16 raw Likert1 for unobserved'. Polish prompt :12/:18 consistently uses binary0. No binary craft criterion and no likert block with a missing anchor exists. Counterexample search: (a) broken app passing — a visually crude but functional app cannot get top visual credit because each likert anchor 1-3 describes the specific degradation; a dead shell gets Likert 1 (normalized 0) per visual/prompt.md:12. (b) conforming alternative failing — a polished app with a different style is not penalised by type choice; visual/prompt.md:14 says layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice. Minor observation (not a type defect): hro_pol_earlier_place (polish/judge.toml:41) uses a 'within a few pixels' tolerance on a binary row; this is a threshold wording issue for other rows (tool feasibility/clarity), not a mismatch of binary vs likert. Unverified: the Likert-1-to-zero normalization happens inside RewardKit (score.py consumes already-normalized dimension rewards; score.py:16-48), so I did not observe it; this row does not depend on runtime measurement and no run was executed by this reviewer.
